# Sanctum Runtime — Complete LLM Documentation
# https://www.sanctumruntime.com/llms-full.txt
# Updated: 2026-06-03
# Format: plain text, section-delimited, machine-readable
# Short index: https://www.sanctumruntime.com/llms.txt

This file contains the complete documentation for Sanctum Runtime, including
platform overview, API reference, SDK reference, policy engine, architecture,
pricing, security model, use cases, and all blog articles.

It is intended for large language models, AI assistants, and developer tools
that need to understand how Sanctum Runtime works without crawling multiple pages.

================================================================================
SECTION 1: WHAT IS SANCTUM RUNTIME
================================================================================

Sanctum Runtime is open-source middleware that sits between AI reasoning and
real-world execution. It is the runtime trust boundary for autonomous systems.

Every meaningful agent — LLM tools, robots, MCP servers, computer-use, workflow
bots — eventually needs a trusted place where a proposed action becomes a
permitted action. Sanctum is that place.

Core principle: Content guardrails protect what the model says. Sanctum protects
what the system does — before side effects happen.

Key capabilities:
- Pre-execution action verification: approve, pause for human review, or block
- Policy engine: unlimited per-action rules with YAML import/export
- Signed action tokens: HMAC-SHA256 proof that an action was approved
- Blast-radius scoring: reversibility, data sensitivity, physical-world impact
- Source-trust classification: indirect prompt injection defense (7 levels)
- Human-in-the-loop: verification queue with resume after operator approval
- Dual approver + auto-escalate: two distinct approvers required for high-risk
- Fleet kill switch: org-wide pause that blocks all actions until resumed
- Policy replay: test current policies against historical audit entries
- SOC2 + NIST AI RMF evidence exports: 16 mapped controls
- 16 framework adapters: LangChain, OpenAI Agents, MCP, CrewAI, ROS2, and more
- Local LLM risk scoring via Ollama — no cloud required
- Domain policy marketplace: healthcare PHI, finance, ROS2 safety, MCP baseline

License: MIT open core
GitHub: https://github.com/Matik103/sanctum-runtime
npm: @sanctum-runtime/sdk
Console: https://console.sanctumruntime.com
API: https://api.sanctumruntime.com
Docs: https://www.sanctumruntime.com/docs

================================================================================
SECTION 2: WHO IT IS FOR
================================================================================

Sanctum Runtime is built for:

Agent builders — LangChain, CrewAI, custom Node/Python agents, MCP servers,
and agentic SaaS. Gate function calling and tool use with approve/verify/block.

Platform engineers — standardize "verify before execute" across products.
One API, one audit trail, one policy layer.

Security-minded teams — policy engine plus audit trail without locking into
a proprietary black box. MIT license, self-hostable.

Local-first developers — Ollama, GGUF, vLLM, or OpenAI-compatible APIs for
risk scoring. Full offline mode with heuristics.

Operators — optional dashboard for human-in-the-loop review, verification
queues, fleet management, and real-time monitoring.

Robotics and physical system builders — same verifyAction() API gates
software and physical-world commands: unlock_door, move_robot, emergency_stop.

================================================================================
SECTION 3: SANCTUM VS GUARDRAILS
================================================================================

"Guardrails" in 2024-2026 typically means content safety on the LLM boundary:
blocking jailbreaks, toxicity, PII in chat, structured output validation.
Tools: OpenAI moderation, Llama Guard, NeMo Guardrails, Azure Content Safety.

That stack is necessary for customer-facing chat. It does not replace a gate
on execution — unlock_door, transfer_funds, delete_production_data, run_shell.

Sanctum adds the action layer:

  User / sensor input
        |
        v
  Content guardrails    — jailbreak, toxicity, PII in chat
        |
        v
  Model plans an action
        |
        v
  Sanctum Runtime       — policy + risk → APPROVE · VERIFY · BLOCK
        |                  audit, webhooks, human approval, resume
        v
  Real execution (email, door, DB, robot, API, ...)

Recommendation: use both. Guardrails on chat; Sanctum on anything that changes
the world.

Comparison:
- Content guardrails stop harmful text.
- Sanctum stops harmful tool/API/robot calls.
- Content guardrails rarely have human approval with resume built in.
- Sanctum has correlationId, resolve, webhooks, and waitForVerification().
- Content guardrails vary on audit trails.
- Sanctum has humanRecord on every decision, audit API, optional Supabase.
- Content guardrails vary on self-hostability.
- Sanctum is MIT, local-first, no account required to try.

When you need Sanctum:
- Essential: agents with privileged tools, robotics/physical access, payments,
  healthcare, infrastructure automation
- High: platform teams standardizing verify-before-execute
- Medium: internal copilots with terminal, file delete, or admin API access
- Lower: read-only chat with no tools (guardrails may suffice)

================================================================================
SECTION 4: HOW IT WORKS — THE DECISION FLOW
================================================================================

  Agent / robot / automation proposes action
        |
        v
  SDK sends POST /v1/actions/verify
  {
    "actor": "agent-1",
    "action": "unlock_door",
    "context": { ... }
  }
        |
        v
  Policy engine evaluates rules
        |
        v
  Risk model scores (Ollama / OpenAI-compatible / heuristics)
        |
        v
  Decision returned:
    APPROVED             — safe to execute
    REQUIRE_VERIFICATION — pause, operator must approve via dashboard or API
    BLOCKED              — deny execution
        |
        v
  If APPROVED and action tokens are configured:
    actionToken returned (HMAC-SHA256, 5 min TTL, scoped to actor+action+org)
        |
        v
  Executor verifies token before running side effect
        |
        v
  Execution outcome reported back (succeeded / failed / skipped)
        |
        v
  Full lifecycle in audit trail

================================================================================
SECTION 5: QUICK START
================================================================================

Clone and run locally:

  git clone https://github.com/Matik103/sanctum-runtime.git
  cd sanctum-runtime
  cp .env.example .env
  npm install
  npm run dev:runtime    # API + dashboard
  npm run smoke          # integration check

Embed via npm:

  npm install @sanctum-runtime/sdk @sanctum-runtime/adapter-agent-runtime

  import { SanctumRuntime } from '@sanctum-runtime/sdk'
  import { protectAgent, AgentActions } from '@sanctum-runtime/adapter-agent-runtime'

  const sanctum = new SanctumRuntime({
    baseUrl: process.env.SANCTUM_API_URL!,
  })

  await protectAgent(sanctum, {
    actor: 'support-bot',
    action: AgentActions.SEND_EMAIL,
    context: { to: 'user@example.com', heard: 'Send them the reset link' },
    execute: async () => sendEmail(),
  })

Python (pip):

  pip install sanctum-runtime

Works without the dashboard. Works with Ollama off (heuristics + policies).
Works self-hosted on your infrastructure.

================================================================================
SECTION 6: RUNTIME API REFERENCE
================================================================================

Base URL: SANCTUM_API_URL (env) or https://api.sanctumruntime.com (cloud)
Auth: X-Sanctum-Key header, or Authorization: Bearer <Supabase JWT>

--- Action Verification ---

POST /v1/actions/verify
  Gate one action before execution.

  Request body:
  {
    "actor": "agent-1",
    "action": "unlock_door",
    "context": {
      "heard": "Open the front door",
      "time": "02:13 AM",
      "owner_sleeping": true,
      "instructionSource": "trusted_user",
      "dataSensitivity": "internal",
      "reversible": false,
      "physicalWorld": true,
      "org_id": "acme"
    },
    "offlineMode": false,
    "correlationId": "run-42"
  }

  Response:
  {
    "id": "uuid",
    "decision": "APPROVED" | "REQUIRE_VERIFICATION" | "BLOCKED",
    "reason": "...",
    "humanRecord": "plain English description",
    "actionToken": { "token": "...", "expiresAt": "..." },
    "blastRadius": { "level": "high", "score": 78, "factors": [...] },
    "sourceTrust": "trusted_user" | "system" | "memory" | "tool_output" | "untrusted_content"
  }

POST /v1/actions/token/verify
  Validate a signed approval token before running side effects.

--- Audit ---

GET /v1/audit?limit=50&org_id=acme
  List audit log entries.

GET /v1/audit/replay?limit=50&org_id=acme
  Replay recent audit events against current policies (shadow test).

POST /v1/audit/:id/resolve
  Approve or deny a pending REQUIRE_VERIFICATION entry.
  Body: { "decision": "approved" | "blocked", "resolvedBy": "...", "note": "..." }

GET /v1/verifications/:correlationId
  Poll verification state: pending / approved / blocked.

--- Policies ---

GET /v1/policies
  List all policies.

POST /v1/policies
  Create or update a policy.
  Body: { "action": "send_email", "requiresVerification": false, "autoBlock": false }

PATCH /v1/policies/:action
  Update policy fields.

DELETE /v1/policies/:action
  Remove policy.

POST /v1/policies/simulate
  Simulate an action without writing an audit entry.

GET /v1/policies/export.yaml
  Export all policies as YAML.

POST /v1/policies/import.yaml
  Import policies from YAML. Body: { "yaml": "...", "merge": true }

GET /v1/orgs/:orgId/policies
  Org-scoped policy view.

--- Evidence / Compliance ---

GET /v1/evidence/summary
  Export action-boundary control evidence for SOC2 / NIST AI RMF audits.

--- Health / Status ---

GET /health
  Liveness check. Returns ok, ollama status, policy count, audit count.

GET /v1/status
  Runtime + risk model + policy stats.

GET /v1/webhooks/status
  Webhook configuration summary.

--- Proxy (Connect Agent) ---

POST /v1/proxy/:platform/chat/completions
  Zero-install proxy for external AI platforms. Supported platforms:
  openai, deepseek, qwen, kimi, doubao, gemini.
  Add header: X-Sanctum-Agent-Token: sk_agent_...
  The proxy forwards to the real platform, streams back, and logs tool calls.

GET /v1/proxy/platforms
  List supported proxy platforms.

--- Agent Tokens (Connect Agent) ---

POST /v1/orgs/:orgId/agent-tokens
  Register a new agent and receive an sk_agent_... token.

DELETE /v1/orgs/:orgId/agent-tokens/:tokenId
  Revoke an agent token.

================================================================================
SECTION 7: SDK REFERENCE (@sanctum-runtime/sdk)
================================================================================

const sanctum = new SanctumRuntime({
  baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:3001',   // or https://api.sanctumruntime.com
  apiKey: process.env.SANCTUM_API_KEY,  // optional
  getAccessToken: async () => jwtOrNull, // optional Supabase integration
})

Core methods:

verifyAction(request, options?)
  Gate one action. Returns decision, actionToken, blastRadius, sourceTrust.

policy(action, 'approve' | 'verify' | 'block')
  Set policy mode shorthand.

registerPolicy(action, modeOrPartialPolicy)
  Create any action policy with full field control.

deletePolicy(action)
  Remove a policy.

getPolicies()
  Fetch all policies.

exportPoliciesYaml()
  Download YAML string of all policies.

importPoliciesYaml(yaml, merge?)
  Import from YAML string.

getAudit(limit?)
  Fetch audit entries.

replayAudit(limit?, orgId?)
  Shadow-test current policies against recent audit entries.

getEvidenceSummary(limit?, orgId?)
  Export action-boundary evidence package.

verifyActionToken(token)
  Verify a signed approval token at the executor boundary.

resolveAuditEntry(id, { decision, resolvedBy?, note? })
  Operator approve/deny a pending verification.

getVerificationStatus(correlationId)
  Single poll for verification state.

waitForVerification(correlationId, { timeoutMs?, pollIntervalMs? })
  Poll until verification resolves (approved / blocked / timeout).

getStatus()
  Runtime status.

getWebhookStatus()
  Webhook configuration.

middleware()
  Express/Fastify middleware pattern: agent.use(sanctum.middleware())

runtime().attach(host)
  Robotics-style attach hook for device/robot hosts.

--- Agent Adapter (@sanctum-runtime/adapter-agent-runtime) ---

import { protectAgent, AgentActions } from '@sanctum-runtime/adapter-agent-runtime'

await protectAgent(sanctum, {
  action: 'unlock_door',
  context: { heard: 'Open the door', org_id: 'acme' },
  correlationId: 'run-123',
  awaitVerification: { timeoutMs: 120_000 },  // wait for dashboard approval
  execute: async () => unlock(),
})

AgentActions constants:
SEND_EMAIL, DELETE_FILE, EXECUTE_TERMINAL, UNLOCK_DOOR, MOVE_ROBOT,
DISABLE_ALARM, MOVE_TO_LOCATION, NAVIGATE, DOCK, CALIBRATE_ARM,
RUN_WORKFLOW, POST_SLACK, UPDATE_CRM, EMERGENCY_STOP, START_LINE,
DISPENSE, MOVE_BED, ACCESS_RECORD, SEND_MESSAGE, STORE_MEMORY, PLACE_ORDER

================================================================================
SECTION 8: POLICY ENGINE
================================================================================

Each policy is keyed by action name — any string. Optional org prefix:
"acme:wire_transfer" with org_id in verify context.

Policy fields:

requiresVerification (boolean)
  Force human review even when risk model says low risk.

autoBlock (boolean)
  Always block this action regardless of context.

blockWhenOffline (boolean)
  Block when operating in heuristics-only / no model mode.

allowedActors (string[])
  Allowlist of actor values allowed to request this action.

riskPrompt (string)
  Custom instructions for the risk model on this specific action.

Policy modes (SDK shorthand):
- approve    → no verify, no block
- verify     → requiresVerification: true
- block      → autoBlock: true

Unknown actions use a permissive default until you register a policy.

YAML format (export/import):

  actions:
    send_email:
      requiresVerification: false
      autoBlock: false
      allowedActors: ["support-bot", "billing-agent"]
      riskPrompt: "Email to external domains should be flagged"
    unlock_door:
      requiresVerification: true
      blockWhenOffline: true
    wire_transfer:
      autoBlock: true

================================================================================
SECTION 9: SIGNED ACTION TOKENS
================================================================================

When SANCTUM_ACTION_TOKEN_SECRET (or fallback signing secret) is configured,
approved actions receive a signed actionToken:

{
  "decision": "APPROVED",
  "actionToken": {
    "token": "eyJ...",
    "expiresAt": "2026-06-03T12:05:00Z"
  }
}

Token is HMAC-SHA256, scoped to: actor + action + org + audit ID, 5 min TTL.

Executor pattern:

  const result = await sanctum.verifyAction(request)
  if (result.decision !== 'APPROVED' || !result.actionToken) {
    throw new Error('not approved')
  }

  // Verify at executor boundary (optional but recommended):
  await sanctum.verifyActionToken(result.actionToken.token)

  await performSideEffect()

  // Report outcome:
  await sanctum.reportActionExecution(result.id, {
    actionToken: result.actionToken.token,
    status: 'succeeded',
    reportedBy: 'gmail.executor',
    resultSummary: 'Email sent to customer@example.com',
    durationMs: 184,
  })

================================================================================
SECTION 10: BLAST-RADIUS SCORING
================================================================================

Every action can be scored for blast radius. Score 0-100, returned on verify.

blastRadius response shape:
{
  "level": "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical",
  "score": 78,
  "reversible": false,
  "dataSensitivity": "internal" | "confidential" | "public",
  "externalDestination": true,
  "physicalWorld": true,
  "estimatedValue": 50000,
  "factors": ["irreversible", "external_recipient", "physical_access"]
}

Pass in context to influence scoring:
- reversible: false (e.g. deleting a file with no backup)
- dataSensitivity: "confidential"
- physicalWorld: true (robotics, smart home, industrial)
- externalDestination: true (emails, API calls leaving the org)
- estimatedValue: 50000 (monetary value of transaction)

Heuristic floors apply — physical-access actions cannot be under-rated by
small local models.

================================================================================
SECTION 11: SOURCE-TRUST CLASSIFICATION (INJECTION DEFENSE)
================================================================================

Every action carries an instructionSource level. Sanctum uses this to elevate
risk automatically when instructions come from untrusted sources.

Source trust levels (most to least trusted):
1. trusted_user        — direct, authenticated user input
2. system              — internal system or scheduled automation
3. memory              — retrieved from agent long-term memory
4. tool_output         — output from a tool/API call (moderate trust)
5. untrusted_content   — retrieved web, email body, user-uploaded docs
6. indirect_injection  — detected indirect prompt injection attempt
7. unknown             — source not declared

Use in verify context:
  "instructionSource": "tool_output"

Sanctum automatically raises blast-radius scoring and may require verification
when source is tool_output or untrusted_content — preventing indirect prompt
injection from silently triggering irreversible actions.

================================================================================
SECTION 12: HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP (HITL)
================================================================================

When a policy sets requiresVerification: true or the risk model returns
REQUIRE_VERIFICATION, the action pauses.

Operator resolves via:
1. Dashboard — review queue at console.sanctumruntime.com
2. API — POST /v1/audit/:id/resolve { "decision": "approved", "note": "..." }

Agent waits via:
  await sanctum.waitForVerification(correlationId, { timeoutMs: 120_000 })

Or with protectAgent():
  await protectAgent(sanctum, {
    action: 'transfer_funds',
    awaitVerification: { timeoutMs: 120_000 },
    execute: async () => transfer(),
  })

Webhooks fire on state transitions:
- verification.required → operator notified
- verification.resolved → agent continues or gets blocked

================================================================================
SECTION 13: WEBHOOKS
================================================================================

Configuration:
  SANCTUM_WEBHOOK_URL=https://your-app.com/sanctum/events
  SANCTUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=optional-signing-secret
  SANCTUM_WEBHOOK_EVENTS=verification.required,action.blocked,verification.resolved

Events:
- verification.required — decision was REQUIRE_VERIFICATION
- action.blocked        — decision was BLOCKED
- verification.resolved — operator approved or denied a pending verification

Payload:
  {
    "event": "verification.required",
    "timestamp": "2026-06-03T12:00:00Z",
    "entry": { /* full audit record */ }
  }

Signature (when SANCTUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET set):
  X-Sanctum-Signature: sha256=<hmac>

================================================================================
SECTION 14: RISK MODEL CONFIGURATION
================================================================================

Sanctum supports three risk model providers:

Ollama (local):
  SANCTUM_RISK_PROVIDER=ollama (or omit, Ollama is default if OLLAMA_URL set)
  OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434
  OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5-3b-instruct  (or llama3.2, mistral, any GGUF model)

OpenAI-compatible (cloud or vLLM/LiteLLM/Groq):
  SANCTUM_RISK_PROVIDER=openai
  OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
  OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1  (or your vLLM endpoint)
  OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini

Heuristics only (no model):
  SANCTUM_RISK_PROVIDER=none
  (or SANCTUM_OFFLINE_MODE=true per-request)

Override model name:
  SANCTUM_RISK_MODEL=llama3.2:3b

================================================================================
SECTION 15: AUDIT TRAIL
================================================================================

Every verify call creates an audit entry:

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "action": "unlock_door",
  "actor": "security-agent",
  "decision": "REQUIRE_VERIFICATION",
  "reason": "Late night access + owner sleeping",
  "humanRecord": "Security agent requested to unlock the front door at 2:13 AM while the owner was sleeping. Decision: held for verification.",
  "context": { ... },
  "correlationId": "run-42",
  "createdAt": "2026-06-03T02:13:00Z",
  "resolvedAt": null,
  "humanResolution": null
}

Storage:
- Local: data/audit.jsonl (default)
- Cloud: Supabase audit_events table (optional, set SUPABASE_* vars)

Narrative context keys for human-readable records:
- heard, user_said, spoken_command — what was said
- intent, goal — stated purpose
- prompt, instruction — prompt/injection text
- channel, source — voice, api, webhook, etc.

Export:
  GET /v1/audit         — JSON list
  GET /v1/evidence/summary — compliance-mapped evidence package

================================================================================
SECTION 16: COMPLIANCE (SOC2 + NIST AI RMF)
================================================================================

Sanctum exports 16 mapped controls across GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE:

GOVERN:
  GV.OC-1 — Organizational context (policy registry, action catalog)
  GV.RM-1 — Risk management strategy (blast-radius scoring)
  GV.SC-1 — Cybersecurity supply chain (source-trust classification)

MAP:
  MP.AC-1 — Asset classification (action categories, reversibility flags)
  MP.RM-1 — Risk identification (risk model scoring per action)
  MP.RM-2 — Risk assessment (dual-approver, verification requirements)

MEASURE:
  ME.AE-1 — Adverse event analysis (blocked/verified action counts)
  ME.CM-1 — Continuous monitoring (audit trail, webhook alerts)
  ME.CM-2 — Security metrics (blast-radius distribution, decision rates)

MANAGE:
  MN.RS-1 — Incident response (fleet kill switch, manual resolve)
  MN.RS-2 — Recovery (policy replay for post-incident analysis)
  MN.IM-1 — Improvements (policy update audit, version history)

Evidence export: GET /v1/evidence/summary
Returns: control descriptions, implementation evidence, audit samples,
decision statistics, and policy configuration snapshots.

================================================================================
SECTION 17: CONNECT AGENT (ZERO-INSTALL PROXY)
================================================================================

Sanctum includes a zero-install proxy for external AI platforms. External agents
set base_url to the Sanctum proxy and add their agent token. Sanctum forwards
to the real platform, streams back, and logs all tool calls.

Supported platforms: openai, deepseek, qwen, kimi, doubao, gemini

Anthropic/Claude uses a proprietary protocol and is not compatible with this
proxy. Use the Sanctum SDK directly for Claude agents.

Setup:
1. Register an agent at console.sanctumruntime.com → Agents → Register
2. Copy your sk_agent_... token
3. At console.sanctumruntime.com → Connect Agent, save your platform API key

Agent configuration (Python):
  from openai import OpenAI

  client = OpenAI(
      base_url="https://api.sanctumruntime.com/v1/proxy/openai",
      api_key="<your-openai-api-key>",
      default_headers={
          "X-Sanctum-Agent-Token": "sk_agent_...",
      },
  )

Agent configuration (TypeScript):
  import OpenAI from 'openai'

  const client = new OpenAI({
    baseURL: 'https://api.sanctumruntime.com/v1/proxy/deepseek',
    apiKey: '<your-deepseek-api-key>',
    defaultHeaders: {
      'X-Sanctum-Agent-Token': 'sk_agent_...',
    },
  })

The proxy:
- Streams responses (SSE) with full compatibility
- Accumulates tool call arguments across delta chunks
- Logs complete tool calls to the audit trail
- Enforces rate limits: 600 req/min per agent token, 200 req/min anonymous
- Requires no SDK changes — just change base_url

================================================================================
SECTION 18: FLEET KILL SWITCH
================================================================================

Operator-triggered org-wide pause. When activated, every verify call returns
BLOCKED until the operator resumes.

Use case: incident response — immediately stop all agents, robots, and
automations in your organization while you investigate.

Activate: Dashboard → Fleet → Emergency Stop (or API endpoint)
Resume: Dashboard → Fleet → Resume (or API endpoint)

During pause: all verify calls return { "decision": "BLOCKED", "reason": "fleet_paused" }

================================================================================
SECTION 19: DUAL APPROVER + AUTO-ESCALATE
================================================================================

For high-risk actions, require two distinct human approvers before execution:

Policy:
  {
    "action": "wire_transfer",
    "requireSecondApprover": true,
    "escalationAfterMinutes": 10,
    "escalationRole": "admin"
  }

Behavior:
- First approval queues the action for second review
- If no second approval within escalationAfterMinutes, escalated to escalationRole
- Execution only proceeds after both approvals
- Both approvals logged in audit trail with approver identity

================================================================================
SECTION 20: ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
================================================================================

Required:
  HOST                    API listen hostname (default 127.0.0.1)
  PORT                    API listen port (default 3001)
  SANCTUM_API_URL         Client-side API URL (for SDK consumers)

Risk model:
  SANCTUM_RISK_PROVIDER   ollama | openai | none
  OLLAMA_URL              http://127.0.0.1:11434
  OLLAMA_MODEL            qwen2.5-3b-instruct
  OPENAI_API_KEY          sk-... (for openai provider)
  OPENAI_BASE_URL         https://api.openai.com/v1
  OPENAI_MODEL            gpt-4o-mini
  SANCTUM_RISK_MODEL      Override model name
  SANCTUM_OFFLINE_MODE    true = heuristics only (no model)

Security:
  SANCTUM_API_KEY         Lock down the API (X-Sanctum-Key header)
  SANCTUM_API_KEY_PEPPER  Salt for API key hashing
  SANCTUM_ACTION_TOKEN_SECRET  HMAC secret for signed action tokens
  SANCTUM_SECRETS_KEY     AES-256-GCM key for encrypting stored credentials
  SANCTUM_WEBHOOK_SECRET  HMAC secret for webhook signatures

Webhooks:
  SANCTUM_WEBHOOK_URL     https://your-app.com/sanctum/events
  SANCTUM_WEBHOOK_EVENTS  verification.required,action.blocked,verification.resolved

Supabase (optional cloud persistence):
  SUPABASE_URL            Your Supabase project URL
  SUPABASE_ANON_KEY       Supabase anon key
  SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY  Supabase service role key

Rate limiting:
  SANCTUM_RATE_LIMIT_AGENT_TOKEN  req/min per agent token (default 600)
  UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS             proxy upstream timeout (default 25000)

Dashboard:
  DASHBOARD_HOST          Dashboard listen hostname
  DASHBOARD_PORT          Dashboard listen port
  VITE_SANCTUM_API_URL    API URL baked into dashboard build

================================================================================
SECTION 21: 12 CATEGORIES — ONE RUNTIME
================================================================================

The same verifyAction() API gates software and physical actions.

Category 1: AI Agents
  Example actions: send_email, delete_file, execute_terminal, tool calls, MCP calls
  Example context: heard, intent, tool args, instructionSource
  Adapter: @sanctum-runtime/adapter-agent-runtime (protectAgent)
  Frameworks: LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents, Mastra, AutoGen, LlamaIndex,
              smolagents, Pydantic AI, Vercel AI, n8n, Zapier

Category 2: Humanoids
  Example actions: unlock_door, move_to_location, handover_object, grasp
  Example context: location, owner_sleeping, time, near_human
  Use: blast-radius scoring for physical actions, dual approver for high-risk

Category 3: Embodied AI
  Example actions: move_robot, grasp, release_payload, navigate_zone
  Example context: zone, speed, near_human, sensor_flags

Category 4: Smart Home
  Example actions: unlock_door, disable_alarm, set_thermostat, stream_camera
  Example context: device_id, room, user_home, time
  Policy: require verification for lock/alarm actions when owner away

Category 5: AI Operating Systems (Computer Use)
  Example actions: delete_file, install_package, kill_process, run_shell
  Example context: path, privilege, user_id
  Use: verify before any destructive file or process operations

Category 6: Robotics Integrators (ROS2, AMR, Warehouse)
  Example actions: navigate, dock, calibrate_arm, emergency_stop
  Example context: map_id, battery_pct, sensor_flags, zone
  Adapter: sanctum.runtime().attach(host) for ROS2 action servers

Category 7: Workflow Automation
  Example actions: run_workflow, post_slack, update_crm, trigger_webhook
  Example context: workflow_id, tenant, trigger, external_destination
  Frameworks: n8n, Zapier, CrewAI, custom automation pipelines

Category 8: Physical Security / Edge
  Example actions: open_gate, arm_perimeter, stream_camera, unlock_access
  Example context: site_id, operator, offline, auth_level

Category 9: Healthcare Robotics
  Example actions: dispense, move_bed, access_record, administer
  Example context: patient_zone, role, policy_id, phi_involved
  Policy pack: healthcare-phi marketplace template

Category 10: Autonomous Mobility
  Example actions: change_route, engage_autonomous_mode, open_door
  Example context: route_id, occupancy, weather, speed

Category 11: AI Companions
  Example actions: send_message, store_memory, place_order, share_data
  Example context: channel, user_id, consent, data_sensitivity

Category 12: Industrial Automation
  Example actions: emergency_stop, start_line, adjust_setpoint, open_valve
  Example context: line_id, shift, safety_interlock, zone

================================================================================
SECTION 24: SECURITY MODEL
================================================================================

Authentication:
- Dashboard: Supabase JWT (email/password or OAuth)
- API from agents: X-Sanctum-Key header (hashed with SANCTUM_API_KEY_PEPPER)
- Agent proxy: sk_agent_... token (HMAC-SHA256 with SANCTUM_API_KEY_PEPPER)
- Connect proxy: X-Sanctum-Agent-Token header

Credential storage:
- Platform API keys: AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest
- Key derived from SANCTUM_SECRETS_KEY via SHA-256
- Format: iv:tag:ciphertext (hex-encoded)
- Keys never logged, never returned after save

Rate limiting:
- Agent tokens: 600 req/min per token (configurable via SANCTUM_RATE_LIMIT_AGENT_TOKEN)
- Anonymous/IP: 200 req/min
- Per-route limits on sensitive endpoints

Audit immutability:
- Entries append-only in local JSONL
- Supabase mirror with RLS (each user owns their rows)
- Correlation IDs link related events

Org isolation:
- All API handlers check org membership via resolveOrgScope + assertOrgAllowed
- Cross-org writes are rejected at the middleware layer

Action token security:
- HMAC-SHA256 signed, 5 min TTL
- Scoped to actor + action + org + audit ID
- Executor must verify before any side effect

Source-trust classification:
- Untrusted content and tool output automatically elevate risk
- Indirect prompt injection defense at the policy layer

Hardware attestation (enterprise):
- TPM2, software-sealed, SGX
- Runtime identity verification before connect

================================================================================
SECTION 28: GLOSSARY
================================================================================

Runtime
  The execution layer that intercepts actions before side effects occur.

Trusted runtime
  A runtime that enforces policy, signs decisions, and produces audit evidence.

Action verification
  The API call to POST /v1/actions/verify that returns APPROVED, BLOCKED, or
  REQUIRE_VERIFICATION before a side effect runs.

Policy
  A per-action rule set specifying whether to approve, verify, or block.
  Keyed by action name (string). Supports org prefixes (acme:send_email).

Blast radius
  Scoring of an action's potential impact: reversibility, data sensitivity,
  physical-world effect, external destination, monetary value.

Source trust
  Classification of where instructions came from. Untrusted sources elevate
  risk automatically — indirect prompt injection defense.

Action token
  HMAC-SHA256 signed proof that an action was approved. Short-lived (5 min TTL).
  Executors must verify before running side effects.

Human-in-the-loop (HITL)
  An approval workflow where a human operator must review and approve an action
  before the agent continues execution.

Correlation ID
  A client-supplied ID linking related audit events (the original request,
  verification state, resolution, and execution outcome).

Fleet kill switch
  Org-wide emergency pause. All verify calls return BLOCKED until resumed.

Dual approver
  Policy requiring two distinct human approvals before an action executes.

Policy replay
  Testing current policies against historical audit entries to preview what
  would change if policies were applied yesterday.

Blast-radius scoring
  See blast radius above. Score 0-100 with level (low/medium/high/critical).

Embodied AI
  AI acting in physical systems — robots, IoT devices, industrial controls.

Agent
  Autonomous software proposing actions (LLM with tools, workflow bot,
  robot controller, MCP server).

Open core
  MIT-licensed local runtime (this repo). Enterprise hosted features in
  a separate commercial track.

Orchestration
  Coordinating multiple agents and runtimes across a fleet with shared policies.

Attestation
  Hardware-backed proof of runtime identity (TPM2, SGX, or software-sealed).

Control plane
  The hosted dashboard + API for operator management (console.sanctumruntime.com).

Connect Agent
  Sanctum's zero-install proxy for external AI platforms. Change base_url to
  route through Sanctum without installing an SDK.

================================================================================
SECTION 29: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
================================================================================

Q: Is Sanctum only for AI agents?
A: No. Sanctum gates any autonomous system: AI agents, robots, smart home
devices, industrial PLCs, workflow automations, computer use, and more.
The same verifyAction() API works for all 12 categories.

Q: Do I need to use the dashboard?
A: No. The SDK and REST API work standalone. The dashboard is optional.

Q: Does it work with local/offline models?
A: Yes. Set OLLAMA_URL and OLLAMA_MODEL to use a local Ollama instance.
Set SANCTUM_OFFLINE_MODE=true for heuristics-only (no model at all).

Q: Can I self-host?
A: Yes. Full self-host instructions in HOSTED.md and RENDER.md. MIT license.

Q: Does Sanctum replace content guardrails (NeMo, Llama Guard, etc.)?
A: No — they solve different problems. Use content guardrails on chat/LLM
outputs. Use Sanctum on tool calls, APIs, robots, and anything that changes
the world. Use both.

Q: How is Sanctum different from just building an if/else policy in my agent?
A: Server-side enforcement (can't be bypassed by prompt injection), signed
audit trail, human-approval workflow with resume, blast-radius scoring,
policy replay for post-incident analysis, org-level fleet management.

Q: What happens if the Sanctum API is down?
A: Set blockWhenOffline: true on sensitive policies to fail safe.
Or use offlineMode: true for heuristics-only decisions.

Q: Can I use multiple agent tokens?
A: Yes. Each registered agent gets its own sk_agent_... token. Tokens can be
rotated or revoked individually.

Q: What AI platforms does the Connect Agent proxy support?
A: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Doubao, Gemini.
Anthropic/Claude requires the Sanctum SDK directly.

Q: Is the audit log tamper-proof?
A: Local JSONL is append-only by convention. Supabase mirror has RLS.
Enterprise tier adds cryptographic audit signing.
